ours: angle DAE = (1/2)(angle C - angle B), proved with the order C, D, E, B along seg CB as figure 3.63 draws it
note: Proof question, so the key prints nothing - but the STEM carries a defect found while solving it, recorded separately in the errata file. The printed betweenness 'C - E - D' contradicts figure 3.63, which draws D between C and E, and it also contradicts the result the same question asks to be proved. Established three independent ways: (a) the rendered figure places the right-angle mark and the dashed seg AD above E on seg CB; (b) algebraically, order B-E-D-C gives angle DAE = (1/2)(angle B - angle C); (c) a numeric sweep over four triangles measured angle DAE in a coordinate model and reported the betweenness at the same time - B=44/C=58, B=30/C=95 and B=70/C=71 all produce order C-D-E and the value (1/2)(C-B), while B=80/C=40 produces order C-E-D and the value (1/2)(B-C). So 'C - E - D' occurs precisely when angle B > angle C, which makes the printed expression (1/2)(angle C - angle B) negative. Not counted as BOOK-KEY-WRONG because the ANSWERS section prints no entry for this question; it is a stem defect, not a key defect.
